anchors.description: Long (11 in) edge of the white worksheet lying flat on the foreground round table, measured between the sheet's two left-side corners
anchors.visible_evidence: A single white rectangular sheet lies flat on the round table below the camera; its four corners are visible as a sharp parallelogram. The edge chosen runs in the image depth (foreshortened) direction: its projected length (about 43 px) exceeds what the sheet's short 8.5 in side could produce under the measured tabletop foreshortening, so it is the 11 in side.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Assumed a US letter sheet (8.5x11 in, 0.2794 m long edge) in a US classroom; an A4 sheet would give 0.297 m (+6%). A thin stack rather than one sheet would enlarge the visible footprint by a few percent. Corners localized to about +/-2 px.

anchors.description: Length of the luminous lens of the ceiling fluorescent troffer, measured along its near long edge from the left end of the panel to its right end
anchors.visible_evidence: Rectangular fluorescent troffer in the ceiling at upper left, with a straight high-contrast boundary between the bright luminous lens and the darker ceiling along its near long edge; both ends of that edge are visible (the far long edge is clipped by the image top).
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Assumed the standard US 2x4 ft troffer (1.22 m overall), whose luminous aperture is about 1.16 m; a 3 ft (0.91 m) fixture would be about 20% shorter. The measured edge is the visible lens aperture, not the fixture frame, and the image is overexposed along this edge (+/-3 px).
